```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```



```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)



lul_d<-read_csv('../data/life-under-lockdown-wave2-extract.csv')
   col_types=cols(
     col_integer(),
     col_factor(),
     col_factor(levels = c(
       'Nothing at all',
       'Not very nuch',
       'A fair amount',
       'A great deal'
     )),
     col_integer()
   )

```

```{r}
lul_d%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=gender))+
  geom_bar()
```

```{r}
lul_d%>%
  count(gender)%>% kable()
```
```{r}
lul_d%>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x=beliefs)
  )+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1)

```
```{r}
lul_d%>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    Mdn=median(beliefs),
    m=mean(beliefs),
    SD=sd(beliefs),
  )%>%
  kable(digits = 2)
  
```

#Hypothesis 
gender is associated with mean number if misinformation beliefs
```{r}
lul_d%>%
  group_by(gender)%>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    Mdn=median(beliefs),
    m=mean(beliefs),
    SD=sd(beliefs),
  )%>%
  kable(digits = 2)


```
There were too few people who indentified in another way for them to be included in the full analysis. Males had slightly more misinformation beliefs (M=0.73, SD=1.13) than female (M=0.61, SD=1.05),but this was not statistically significant, t(494.31)=-1.201, p=0,230.

```{r}
lul_d%>%
  filter(gender!='In another way')%>%
  t.test(
    formula=beliefs~gender,
    var.equal=FALSE,
    data=.
  )


```
